prompt.context_jp: けれど彼女の視線の先には、湯気を立てる小さな包み___あった。
prompt.prompt_jp: けれど彼女の視線の先には、湯気を立てる小さな包み___あった。
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the particle that best fits.

feedback.correct_en: The 包み is newly introduced into the scene — An suddenly notices it. New-information existence uses が.
feedback.incorrect_en: は would treat the package as an already established topic, which it isn't here — it's being spotted for the first time.

contrast_examples.en: There's a book on the desk. (new info)

contrast_examples.jp: その本は机の上にある。
contrast_examples.en: That book (topic) is on the desk.

prompt.context_jp: 五十嵐の腕___反射的に動き、患者の頭を支えた。
prompt.prompt_jp: 五十嵐の腕___反射的に動き、患者の頭を支えた。
prompt.prompt_en: Which particle fits best?

feedback.correct_en: This is a sudden, narrated event — his arm (new, momentary subject) moves reflexively. が marks that unprepared, event-level subject.
feedback.incorrect_en: は would make 'his arm' a general topic being commented on, losing the sense of a sudden reflex.

contrast_examples.en: My hand moved on its own. (event)

prompt.context_jp: 「灰島院長___打ち出した 新しい方針のせいよ」
prompt.prompt_jp: 灰島院長___打ち出した 新しい方針のせいよ。
prompt.prompt_en: Which particle fits in this relative clause?

feedback.correct_en: Inside a relative clause modifying 方針, the subject takes が. は almost never appears as the relative-clause subject here.
feedback.incorrect_en: は would break the clause structure — it would try to make 灰島院長 the sentence-level topic, not the modifier's subject.

contrast_examples.en: My father made a dish. (main clause topic)

prompt.context_jp: 「もう 我々 脳外に できること___ないからね」
prompt.prompt_jp: もう 我々 脳外に できること___ないからね。
prompt.prompt_en: Which particle fits here?

feedback.correct_en: This is contrastive は: 'as for what WE (neurosurgery) can do, there's nothing (though other departments might).' The contrast with other specialties is implicit.
feedback.incorrect_en: が would make it a flat existential statement and lose the contrastive nuance that the doctor is washing his hands of this case.

contrast_examples.jp: 私にはできない(けど他の人なら…)。
contrast_examples.en: I can't do it (but maybe others...) - contrast

prompt.context_jp: 一平の口から漏れた過去の断片___、五十嵐の呼吸を止めた。
prompt.prompt_jp: 一平の口から漏れた過去の断片___、五十嵐の呼吸を止めた。
prompt.prompt_en: Which particle fits best?

feedback.correct_en: A specific, newly-introduced subject (the fragments that just slipped out) causes an event. が marks this event-level subject.
feedback.incorrect_en: は would frame it as an established topic being described, but the fragments are a one-time trigger, not a topic.

prompt.context_jp: 「僕___ 今 こうやって 一緒に働けてるだけで十分です」
prompt.prompt_jp: 僕___ 今 こうやって 一緒に働けてるだけで十分です。
prompt.prompt_en: Which particle fits for Igarashi stating his own view?

feedback.correct_en: Igarashi is stating his personal position/feeling — 'as for me…' Topic は is natural for first-person statements of stance.
feedback.incorrect_en: が would sound like he's identifying who finds it enough (as if answering 'who?'), which isn't what the moment calls for.

contrast_examples.en: I'll do it (exhaustive — I'm the one).

prompt.context_jp: 廊下を走る五十嵐の顔に、汗___滲んでいた。
prompt.prompt_jp: 廊下を走る五十嵐の顔に、汗___滲んでいた。
prompt.prompt_en: Which particle fits?

feedback.correct_en: Descriptive, visible new state: sweat appearing on his face. Sensory/observational descriptions take が.
feedback.incorrect_en: は would need sweat to already be a topic under discussion — but it's a fresh detail the narrator is painting.

contrast_examples.en: As for tears, I have none left.

prompt.context_jp: 「放射線科医のあなた___ 画像を読影するのが仕事でしょ」
prompt.prompt_jp: 放射線科医のあなた___ 画像を読影するのが仕事でしょ。
prompt.prompt_en: Which particle fits?

feedback.correct_en: The speaker is defining the listener's role: 'as for you, a radiologist, your job is...' — classic topic-comment with は.
feedback.incorrect_en: が would identify WHO reads images (as if answering 'who?'), but here he's prescribing a role to a known person.

contrast_examples.en: YOU are the one who does it. (identification)

prompt.context_jp: 広瀬の目に、光___ひとつ灯ったように見えた。
prompt.prompt_jp: 広瀬の目に、光___ひとつ灯ったように見えた。
prompt.prompt_en: Which particle fits?

feedback.correct_en: A newly-appearing, observed phenomenon (a light flickering) — descriptive sentences use が for the observed subject.
feedback.incorrect_en: は would presuppose '光' as an already-shared topic, clashing with the fresh observational tone.

contrast_examples.en: A star shone in the sky. (observed)

prompt.context_jp: 「私___ 無理だと思います」
prompt.prompt_jp: 私___ 無理だと思います。
prompt.prompt_en: An is backing down — which particle fits?

feedback.correct_en: '私には無理' is the set pattern for 'it's impossible FOR me' — marking the person for whom something is impossible with には.
feedback.incorrect_en: が would make '私' the subject of 無理, but 無理 attaches to the experiencer via に (+は for topic/contrast).

contrast_examples.en: (sounds off — identifying 'I' as the impossible one)

prompt.context_jp: 「“どんな病気___見つける お医者さんになりたい”って」
prompt.prompt_jp: どんな病気___見つける お医者さんになりたい。
prompt.prompt_en: Which particle fits?

feedback.correct_en: 'どんな〜も' is the fixed pattern for 'any kind of ~' — it replaces を here to mean 'find any illness whatsoever.'
feedback.incorrect_en: を alone would just say 'find an illness,' losing the sweeping 'any' meaning that defines An's dream.

prompt.context_jp: 「甘春先生が抱いた夢に憧れて その夢を応援したくて ずっと頑張ってきた人___いるんです」
prompt.prompt_jp: ずっと頑張ってきた人___いるんです。
prompt.prompt_en: Which particle fits?

feedback.correct_en: Introducing the existence of someone new to An's awareness — existential 〜がいる uses が.
feedback.incorrect_en: は would presuppose this person is already a topic, but Hirose is revealing their existence for the first time.

prompt.context_jp: 「ファブリー病___ Ｘ連鎖の遺伝性疾患」
prompt.prompt_jp: ファブリー病___ Ｘ連鎖の遺伝性疾患。
prompt.prompt_en: Which particle fits when defining a disease?

feedback.correct_en: Definitional/explanatory 'A is B' takes は — 'Fabry disease IS an X-linked disorder.'
feedback.incorrect_en: が would answer 'which disease is X-linked?' (exhaustive), not define Fabry itself.

contrast_examples.en: It's whales that are mammals. (exhaustive answer)

prompt.context_jp: 「確かに1人___無理です でも チームなら できるんじゃないですか？」
prompt.prompt_jp: 確かに1人___無理です。でも チームなら できるんじゃないですか？
prompt.prompt_en: Which particle fits with the 'but' contrast?

feedback.correct_en: Contrastive は after で sets up 'alone, no — but as a team, yes.' The explicit でも in the next clause confirms the contrast.
feedback.incorrect_en: 1人が would read as 'one person is impossible,' which doesn't give the contrastive scope needed.

contrast_examples.jp: 一人では無理だが二人ならできる。
contrast_examples.en: Alone it's impossible, but together we can.

prompt.context_jp: 「すぐに頭部ＣＴ___」
prompt.prompt_jp: すぐに頭部ＣＴ___。
prompt.prompt_en: Which particle fits for the imaging order?

feedback.correct_en: The implied verb is 撮る/お願いします — 頭部CT is its direct object, marked by を.
feedback.incorrect_en: が would mark CT as a subject, which doesn't fit a command/request structure.

contrast_examples.en: A CT is needed. (subject of 必要)

prompt.context_jp: 辻村は缶コーヒーを差し出し、五十嵐の隣___並んで立った。
prompt.prompt_jp: 辻村は缶コーヒーを差し出し、五十嵐の隣___並んで立った。
prompt.prompt_en: Which particle fits with 並んで立った?

feedback.correct_en: Location of existence/standing with 立つ uses に — it marks the spot where he ended up standing next to Igarashi.
feedback.incorrect_en: で would mark a location of action; 立つ as 'be positioned' pairs more naturally with に, especially for '~の隣に並ぶ.'

prompt.context_jp: 「これは 左中大脳動脈の血栓閉塞 すぐに血栓を ___する必要があります」
prompt.prompt_jp: すぐに血栓を___する必要があります。
prompt.prompt_en: Which verb fits for removing a thrombus?

feedback.correct_en: 血栓回収 (thrombectomy / clot retrieval) is the standard medical collocation for pulling out a clot.
feedback.incorrect_en: 回復 means 'recovery' (what the patient does), and 回答 means 'answer.' Neither fits a physical clot removal.

prompt.context_jp: 「___を投げたってわけか」
prompt.prompt_jp: ___を投げたってわけか。
prompt.prompt_en: Which word completes the idiom 'to give up'?

feedback.correct_en: さじを投げる literally 'throw the spoon' — a set idiom meaning a doctor gave up on a case. Perfect fit for Onodera's comment.
feedback.incorrect_en: はし (chopsticks) has no such idiom, and 手を投げる isn't standard — 手を引く would mean withdraw, but the set form here is さじ.

contrast_examples.en: The doctor gave up (on the patient).

prompt.context_jp: 「余計なことは しないで___！」
prompt.prompt_jp: 余計なことは しないで___！
prompt.prompt_en: Which ending creates the sharp 'please don't do X' tone?

feedback.correct_en: 〜していただきたい delivered sharply is the cold, formal rebuke the senior doctor uses — polite surface, hostile edge.
feedback.incorrect_en: もらえる is a question form (can I get...), and ください is softer and less cutting than the aggressive いただきたい here.

contrast_examples.en: I'd like you to shut up. (cold-formal)

prompt.context_jp: 「どんな病気であっても 私が___」
prompt.prompt_jp: どんな病気であっても 私が___。
prompt.prompt_en: Which verb captures 'I'll be there for you'?

feedback.correct_en: 寄り添う means 'to stand close by in support' — the exact empathetic image of a doctor beside their patient.
feedback.incorrect_en: 寄りかかる means 'lean on' (the opposite — seeking support), and 近づく is just 'approach,' without the emotional accompaniment.

prompt.context_jp: 「ご自分の将来を ___振るおつもりなんですか？」
prompt.prompt_jp: ご自分の将来を ___振るおつもりなんですか？
prompt.prompt_en: Which word completes 'throw away one's future'?

feedback.correct_en: 棒に振る is the fixed idiom 'to waste/throw away (one's chances, future).' Haijima uses it to pressure An.
feedback.incorrect_en: 水に流す means 'let bygones be bygones,' and 風に is not an idiom here — neither means 'squander.'

prompt.context_jp: 「結局 最後に 人を巻き込み動かすのは 誰かの___」
prompt.prompt_jp: 人を巻き込み動かすのは 誰かの___。
prompt.prompt_en: Which noun best captures what moves people?

feedback.correct_en: 熱意 (passion/zeal) is what Kaburaki credits for pulling people in — fitting the 'magma' metaphor that follows.
feedback.incorrect_en: 注意 (caution) and 用意 (preparation) don't convey the emotional heat that moves others.

prompt.context_jp: 「文句があるなら 技師長に___ください」
prompt.prompt_jp: 文句があるなら 技師長に___ください。
prompt.prompt_en: Which verb fits in this cheeky pushback?

feedback.correct_en: 文句を言う is the standard collocation for 'to complain.' Tamaki is firing back with a set phrase.
feedback.incorrect_en: 話す is just 'talk,' and 述べる is formal 'state' — neither pairs idiomatically with 文句.

prompt.context_jp: 「点ではなく線で___」
prompt.prompt_jp: 点ではなく線で___。
prompt.prompt_en: Which verb completes Igarashi's key insight?

feedback.correct_en: 見る here means 'to view/approach' — see the symptoms as a connected line, not isolated dots. Fits the diagnostic metaphor.
feedback.incorrect_en: 書く (write) and 引く (draw) make literal sense but miss the point: he's telling them how to perceive the data.

contrast_examples.en: See things as a connected line.

prompt.context_jp: Igarashi confesses — 'I like you, as a radiologist.'
prompt.prompt_en: Which phrasing feels most natural for his confession in context?

choices.text: 好きです。僕は、放射線科医として働くあなたが大好きです。
僕は好きです大好きが放射線科医のあなたを。

feedback.correct_en: A is the actual line — the short 好きです lands first, then he qualifies it, ending on 大好きです for emphasis.
feedback.incorrect_en: B scrambles the word order and particles (を on the subject of 好き is wrong). Natural Japanese keeps the 〜が好き frame intact.

prompt.context_jp: Haijima reassures the patient.
prompt.prompt_en: Which phrasing sounds most natural as a hospital director's reassurance?

choices.text: あなたのことは この病院が守ります。
あなたのことを この病院は守ります。

feedback.correct_en: '〜のことは [subject]が守る' topicalizes the patient (what's being protected) and uses が to spotlight THIS hospital as the protector — fitting a reassuring promise.
feedback.incorrect_en: B inverts the particles; 'この病院は' makes the hospital a general topic rather than emphatically asserting it's US who'll protect you.

prompt.context_jp: Igarashi proposes a new role.
prompt.prompt_en: Which phrasing feels most natural for 'isn't this what's needed?'

choices.text: だから必要なんじゃないですか？

feedback.correct_en: 必要 is a na-adjective/noun — you say 必要だ/必要です/必要なんじゃないか. The 〜んじゃないですか tag softens the suggestion.
feedback.incorrect_en: 必要します doesn't exist — 必要 doesn't take する directly in this frame. B is ungrammatical.

prompt.context_jp: An tells Hirose not to worry about it.
prompt.prompt_en: Which is the natural way to say 'don't worry about it'?

choices.text: そんな 気にしないでください。
そんな 心配をしないでください。

feedback.correct_en: 気にしないで is the standard collocation for 'don't worry about it / don't take it to heart' — the actual line An uses.
feedback.incorrect_en: 心配しないで is grammatical but means 'don't be anxious' about something serious; it sounds too heavy for brushing off an apology.

prompt.context_jp: Onodera tells An she can always come back.
prompt.prompt_en: Which phrasing sounds most natural?

choices.text: いつでも戻ってこいな。
いつでも戻ってくるな。

feedback.correct_en: 戻ってこい is the imperative of 戻ってくる — a warm, gruff 'come back anytime' with sentence-final な softening it.
feedback.incorrect_en: 戻ってくるな literally means 'DON'T come back' (negative imperative) — the exact opposite sentiment.
